killSwitch: Set "stage" to 1 and save. That is the whole revert: the preflight goes back to informative and the skill stops requiring it. No code changes, no reinstall, no argument. Rollback from stage 3 goes to 2, never to 1: a publisher problem revokes the publisher requirement, not the preflight one.
requireSignedReceiptsKillSwitch: Set "requireSignedReceipts" to false and save. The verification code stays; gate-publish, reserve-attempt and the publisher simply stop demanding a verified signature. Rollback of the signing requirement never touches the stage.

1.name: informative
1.means: The preflight may be run and read. It blocks nothing.

2.name: preflight required
2.means: A PASS preflight is required before record-evidence. FAIL, UNKNOWN, or a required NOT_RUN stops the flow. Nothing is synchronised, rebased or modified to make it pass.

3.name: persistence and gate-publish required
3.means: Not enabled. Recording evidence, authorising and gate-publish become mandatory before any publication. The controlled publisher at .claude/tools/audit/bin/publish.mjs is the one sanctioned path for that publication: it consumes the lineage's one-shot ticket, runs the exact operation the ticket names, verifies the published bytes, and records the attempt.

honestScope: This is procedural enforcement. The skill instructs an agent to check the gate; nothing here can stop a process that decides not to. It resists mistakes and convenient shortcuts, not a determined actor. The security boundary section of SKILL.md says the same thing and means it.
